chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Waqid Al-Lahham, who said:

I faced Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a road, so I turned my face away from him and passed by. Then I went to him after that and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I meet you but I turn my face away, disliking that it would be grievous upon you.' So he said to me, 'May Allah have mercy on you! A man met me yesterday in such and such a place and said, "Upon you be peace, O Abu Abdillah." How good (is your action), but (his pronouncing it in public was) not beautiful.'
ai.seo_question: What is the rationale behind turning away from the Imam in public according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) by distinguishing between the validity of a greeting and the wisdom of its public delivery during times of political tension. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates Hammad’s subtle avoidance as a prudent measure to prevent burdening the Imam, while gently correcting the man who greeted him loudly, implying that excessive public display can be less aesthetically pleasing or discreet in context. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing religious observance with situational awareness to protect the community and the Imams from undue attention or harm.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Waqad Al Lahaam who said,

‘I met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in a road, but I turned my face away from him<sup>asws</sup> and continued. Then I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> after that, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I met you<sup>asws</sup> but I turned my face away (but I) disliked it that it would be grievous upon you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you! A man met me<sup>asws</sup> yesterday in such and such a place, so he said, ‘Upon you<sup>asws</sup> be the greetings, O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>!’ How good (is your action), but (his pronouncing it in public was) not beautiful’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Hammad ibn Waqid al- Lahham who has said the following:

“Once I came face to face to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) on a road and I turned my face away and passed him by. Later I went to see him and said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I sometimes may turn my face away and pass you so as not to cause you any trouble. ’ The Imam said, ‘May Allah grant you blessings, however, yesterday a man passed by me in such and such place and said, ‘Upon you be peace, O abu ‘Abd Allah.’ What he did was not any good or beautiful.’”
